newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BOLDON THROWS DOWN CHALLENGE TO BAILEY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BOLDON THROWS DOWN CHALLENGE TO BAILEY.

text.p: Ato Boldon confirmed on Saturday his talent is starting to match his ego by equalling the fourth fastest time in history for the 100 metres on the opening day of the sixth world championships.

Assisted by a following wind of 1.3 metres, a fast track and searing heat which did not relent until late in the evening, Boldon clocked 9.87 seconds in his second round heat, the fastest ever time in a qualifying round.
"If you have a lightning fast track, the hot weather and the wind blowing in the right direction, you'll get the year's fastest race," Boldon said.
"That's why I'm telling you, you will probably see a world record tomorrow in the final. My dream is to run the 100 in 9.80 seconds but I'll be happy with 9.81.
"I don't want to insult the record but it's soft and should be lower."

Boldon had enough in reserve to slow down and glance to his left to see the progress of his training partner Maurice Greene, the American champion, who clocked 9.90 for second place and a spot in Sunday's semifinals.
By contrast, Donovan Bailey, the Olympic and world champion and world record holder, made hard work of his second round heat.
Bailey qualified in second place behind American Tim Montgomery but looked in pain as he crossed the line and hobbled from the track.
"It appeared he had a mild cramp in his right leg," said manager Ray Flynn. "But I don't think it's too serious. I think that he's going to be fine to run tomorrow."
American women's champion Marion Jones showed her raw talent for the first time at a major championships in winning both her opening 100 metres races.
"I've been waiting for ever for Sunday to come around," Jones said. "I probably won't get any sleep tonight. It will be the greatest moment of my career if I come away with a world title."
The first gold medal of the championships went to men's shot putter Aleksandr Bagach of Ukraine, who defeated American defending champion John Godina in a tight battle.
Mexican Daniel Garcia took the second gold medal of the evening when he strode through the dusk to win the men's 20 kms walk. Garcia was disqualified at both of the previous two world championships.
Britain's Commonwealth champion Kelly Holmes, one of the gold medal favourites, pulled up 160 metres short of the finishing line in the first round of the women's 1,500 metres.
Holmes sustained calf and Achilles tendon injuries to her left leg and will take no further part in the championships.
Olympic champion Randy Barnes did not qualify for Saturday's shot put final and defending hammer champion Andrei Abduvaliyev also failed to advance.
